name: UIScale
simple: A UIScale makes its parent UI object, and everything inside it, bigger or smaller by multiplying its size. Scale 2 is twice as big, 0.5 is half. Corners, outlines and text inside all grow together, which makes it perfect for 'pop' animations.
analogy: UIScale is like a zoom button on a camera: everything in the picture gets bigger or smaller together, keeping the same layout.
whenToUse: A button that grows a bit when hovered
A menu that pops in by growing from 0 to full size
Making an entire menu smaller on small screens
where: Put it inside the UI object to scale. Create in Studio or with Instance.new in a LocalScript.

terms.modifier: A small invisible object you put INSIDE a UI object to change how it looks or behaves. It does nothing on its own.
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside. A modifier affects its parent.
terms.sibling: Objects that share the same parent, like brothers and sisters.
terms.UDim: Half of a UDim2: just one Scale and one Offset. UDim.new(0, 8) means 0% + 8 pixels. UDim.new(0.1, 0) means 10% of the parent's size.
terms.Scale: A fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size. 0.5 = half.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.Vector2: Two numbers together: X (width or left-right) and Y (height or up-down).
terms.multiplier: A number you multiply by. 2 doubles, 0.5 halves.
terms.AbsoluteSize: The real size in pixels after all the math.
terms.tween: Smoothly animate a value from one number to another over time.

examples.title: Pop a menu open
examples.place: LocalScript inside a Frame (in a ScreenGui in StarterGui)
examples.code:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local menu = script.Parent

local scale = Instance.new("UIScale")
scale.Scale = 0 -- start invisible-tiny
scale.Parent = menu

-- Grow to full size with a little bounce
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
TweenService:Create(scale, info, {Scale = 1}):Play()
explain: Scale 0 makes the menu (and everything in it) zero size.
The tween smoothly changes Scale from 0 to 1 over 0.4 seconds. EasingStyle Back overshoots slightly for a bouncy pop.
A 300x200 menu at Scale 0.5 would be 150x100 pixels.

gotchas: It changes AbsoluteSize, not Size. The Size property stays the same.

UIScale.Scale.simple: The multiplier for the parent's real size. 1 = normal, 2 = double, 0.5 = half. A 200x50 button at Scale 0.5 becomes 100x25 pixels; at 2 it becomes 400x100.
UIScale.Scale.example:
local scale = script.Parent -- a UIScale inside a button
local button = scale.Parent
button.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
	scale.Scale = 1.1 -- 10% bigger on hover
end)
button.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
	scale.Scale = 1
end)
